## Tasks

1.  Read the syllabus and ensure you understand the course procedures and grading.

2.  Download the install the latest versions of R and RStudio. R must be installed first so that RStudio can use it.

    -   R ([Mac OS X](https://mirror.las.iastate.edu/CRAN/) \| [Windows](https://mirror.las.iastate.edu/CRAN/)
    -   RStudio ([Mac OS X](https://rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/#download) \| [Windows](https://rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/#download))

3.  Fix your settings in RStudio to use the [code diagnostics](https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/205753617-Code-Diagnostics).

4.  **IMPORTANT**: Create a [GitHub account](https://github.com/join?source=header-home)

5.  **IMPORTANT** Post your GitHub username on the [GitHub Usernames google sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11mOhk8goCaMc8Uu8wB1CYQLi46jQCSQDH8mvnZnMpT0/edit?usp=sharing). After roughly 10 minutes (during normal working hours), you should receive two emails. One email will be an invitation from "GitHub" to join the BYUI335 organization. Accept the invitation. The other email will be an invitation from "Katie Allen" to collaborate on a repository with your name on it. Accept the invitation. If you do not see the two emails, check your spam folder.

    -   Normally you would create your own repository, but because we want your class repository saved in a special organization we are creating it for you. You will be using this repository to turn in assignments.

6.  Join the Data Science Society workspace in Slack. This is where we will have class conversations and ask questions. Here is the link to join: https://join.slack.com/t/byuidss/signup . The following sub-bullets provide additional detailed instructions about setting up and using slack.

    -   Create a professional username, something you could share with an employer
    -   In addition to the channels you are automatically add to, be sure to join the following two channels:
        -   Our class channel. It will look something like `#ds350_s22_allen` or `#ds350_s22_woodruff`. Find the appropriate channel and add yourself to it. Once you are in the class channel, introduce yourself by replying to the *introduction* thread by clicking the thread, hit reply, then type a brief introduction.
        -   **#tutoring_lab**, add this channel. It is where you can ask questions about code related to specific tasks or case studies.
        -   Browse through the channels and join as as many as you are interested in. This community will be a great resource, even if you are not a Data Science major.
    -   Extra features are available when you install Slack as an app on your PC and/or phone. The more comfortable you become with using Slack, the easier it will be to collaborate with each other throughout your professional career.

7.  Post a professional picture to your GitHub, LinkedIn, and Slack icons. Go to the [BYU-Idaho LinkedIn Photobooth](http://www.byui.edu/alumni/alumni-linkedin-photo-booth) if you don't have a professional picture.

8.  Make plans to attend [Data Science Society](https://mailchi.mp/f2f2078fb178/want-to-deepen-those-analytic-skills-886266) on the second Wednesday of the semester.

9.  Download the R script [first-R-script.R](first-R-script.R) and open it in RStudio. Run each line of code, one at a time (figure out the keyboard shortcut to do this). Note any questions you want to ask your group when you get to class.

    -   It is not crucial that you understand what each line of code does at this point in the semester. However, briefly try guessing what each line of code does before running it, but don't worry if you don't understand all (or any of) the code.

## Readings

Readings teach you to do the things that a data analyst or scientist does and prepare your for the task. There are a lot of readings for this task, but many of them are short.

1.  [Being a better online reader](https://www.newyorker.com/science/maria-konnikova/being-a-better-online-reader)
2.  [Chapter 1 Intro: R for Data Scientists](http://r4ds.had.co.nz/index.html)
3.  [Chapter 4 Basics: R for Data Scientists](https://r4ds.had.co.nz/workflow-basics.html)
4.  [Lesson 3 R and RStudio basics, skip section 3.3](https://rbasics.netlify.app/3-rstudiobasics.html)
5.  [Modern Dive: Chapter 1 Getting Started with Data in R](https://moderndive.com/1-getting-started.html)
6.  Optional: If you are new to R and want more practice, I recommend the 'swirl' package. It is an interactive tutorial. Follow the instructions below:
    -   Run the following code, then follow the prompts. Choose option 1: R programming. When presented with 15 different modules I recommend completing 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 12. (7 and 8 are optional, we will hit them again later in the semester). Say "no" when it asks if you want credit for completing a module.

`install.packages("swirl")`

`library(swirl)`
